title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page: Pi_0 is the free group on two generators, i.e. pi_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. The discrete group G = GL(2,Z)/[Pi_0,Pi_0] is an extension 1 -> M -> G -> H -> 1. Here M = Pi_0^ab is free abelian of rank 2. It is generated by the images lambda_0, lambda_1, lambda_infinity of the loops, with lambda_0 + lambda_1 + lambda_infinity = 0, so M = Z^{0,1,infinity}/diagonal. H = S_3 x mu_2 (identified with T_{0,3}) is a finite group. The rotation rho and transposition sigma act on M by permuting the lambda_i; tau acts by -1.

On this page Grothendieck makes explicit (correcting himself: he 'felt cramped' explaining the construction announced in §50 3°) a group scheme over S_0 = Spec Z fitting into an exact sequence (9):
1 -> M_ -> G_ -> H_{S_0} -> 1.
M_ = V-check(M) is the vector group M (x)_Z G_a, so M_(S) = Gamma(S, O_S (x) M). H_{S_0} is the constant group scheme.

Definition (10). For any scheme S, let G_^Delta(S) be the subgroup of G_(S) that is the inverse image, under G_(S) -> H_S(S) = Gamma(H_S/S), of the 'diagonal' H, i.e. the image of the constant sections H -> Gamma(H_S/S).

Formula (11). By construction G_^Delta(S) is the contracted product (pushout of the extension along M -> Gamma(S, O_S (x) M)) of G with Gamma(S, O_S (x) M). For S = Spec A affine this is G pushed out along M -> M (x) A.

Sequence (12). There is an exact sequence 1 -> A (x) M -> G_^Delta(S) -> H -> 1.

Formula (13). Taking A = Z-hat gives G^ = G_^Delta(Z-hat): the profinite completion of G is obtained as Z-hat-points of the group scheme. He notes this is a general fact for group schemes attached to extensions of discrete groups with abelian kernel.

Purpose (next page): the profinite completion of the metabelian quotient of GL(2,Z) is given a model over Spec Z. On this model he then defines, 'in the schematic framework rather than the profinite one', the automorphism group Z_{rho,sigma} of G-hat^+. Its elements u are given by u(rho) = xi rho and u(sigma) = eta sigma, subject to conditions; existence of alpha and beta is understood locally. This is a metabelian, Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group defined as a group functor on rings, so that one object yields profinite (A = Z-hat) and Q-unipotent-type (A = Q) versions.
errors: No mathematical error. (13) holds because H is finite and M is free of finite rank: the finite-index subgroups of G are cofinal with those containing nM, so G^ is G pushed out along M -> M (x) Z-hat. The 'general fact' needs the hypotheses that the quotient is finite and the kernel finitely generated; they are only implicit.

'Diagonal of Gamma(H_S/S)' means the constant sections. For disconnected S, Gamma(H_S/S) is the group of locally constant maps, and the restriction to constant sections is what makes (12) end in H rather than in Gamma(H_S/S). This is consistent but terse.

ideas.what: Group scheme over Spec Z attached to an extension of a finite group H by a lattice M, obtained by replacing M with the vector group M (x) G_a (pushout of the extension).
ideas.modern_name: Base change / pushout of extensions; a Z-form of the relative (Malcev-type) completion of G relative to G -> H, in the metabelian case
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pushout of extensions is classical. Relative completion is due to Deligne and Hain (Hain, early 1990s).
ideas.where_published: Possibly sketched in the circulated Longue Marche continuation (§49–50); not in EGA/SGA.

ideas.what: Recovering the profinite completion as Z-hat-points of a group scheme over Z: G^ = G_^Delta(Z-hat), with the subfunctor G^Delta cut out by constant H-sections.
ideas.modern_name: Integral model / group-functor interpolation of profinite and pro-unipotent completions

ideas.what: Programme of defining the Teichmüller-type automorphism group Z_{rho,sigma} (a metabelian GT analogue, via generators rho of order 3 and sigma of order 2 of GL2/PSL2(Z)) as a group functor over Spec Z rather than as a profinite group.
ideas.modern_name: Metabelian Grothendieck–Teichmüller group; GT(k) as a functor on rings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT(k) over Q-algebras; Ihara (1985–86) for metabelian Galois representations and the profinite GT; Lochak–Schneps for related work

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the metabelian 'GT-type' group Z_{rho,sigma} as a group functor on all rings over Spec Z. The same object would give the profinite version on Z-hat points and a pro-unipotent-style version on Q-points. By contrast, Drinfeld's GT(k) is defined only over Q-algebras and the profinite GT separately; a single integral model interpolating them is not standard in the literature, at least in the metabelian case.
missed.quote: Nous ferons cependant les constructions dans le cadre schématique, plutôt que profini (next page); Prenant A = Ẑ, on trouve ... 𝔊^∧ ≃ 𝔊^Δ(Ẑ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links Ihara's metabelian (Jacobi-sum) Galois representations with integral or relative-completion frameworks (Hain–Matsumoto). In the metabelian quotient it could give an integral GT-type group scheme whose different points recover the various GT variants.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebra on this page is routine. Its interest is the early (c. 1981+) choice to treat Teichmüller/GT-type automorphism groups of the metabelian quotient of GL2(Z) as group schemes over Spec Z, prefiguring Drinfeld's functorial GT and Hain's relative completion. The fragment is too sketchy to count as a new result.
transcription_corrections: The swirl symbol throughout is the same group 𝔊 as on the neighbouring pages (underlined = group scheme), not 𝔈.
'Pour H schéma S' should read 'Pour tout schéma S'.
In (11), '𝔈^∧_M [-?-]' is most likely the contracted-product notation 𝔊 ∧^M Γ(S, O_S ⊗_Z M), i.e. the pushout of the extension along M -> Γ(S, O_S ⊗ M).
The underbrace in (11) reads '≃ M ⊗_Z A si S affine d'anneau A'.
'(c'est d'ailleurs un fait général sur les schémas en groupes associés à des extensions de groupes discrets à noyau abélien)' — reading confirmed.
The page number at top is 655 or 665 with a corrected digit (written '6[-8-]5'); 'est d'un sens' in the first line is uncertain, plausibly 'est décrite dans' or similar.
